children: Astrotech reported revenue of $274,000 and a net loss of $2.948 million for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, ended September 30, 2026. The company’s operating loss was $3.039 million, while its diluted net loss per share was $1.46. Astrotech reported $11.6 million in working capital at quarter-end.
Revenue was $274,000, compared with $297,000 in the year-ago quarter.
Loss from operations was $3.039 million, compared with $3.536 million.
Net loss was $2.948 million, compared with $3.465 million; diluted net loss per common share was $1.46, versus $2.07.
Working capital was $11.6 million as of September 30, 2026.
The TRACER 1000 was deployed in approximately 38 locations across 17 countries in the United States, Europe, Central America and Asia.

Astrotech and Skycorp Incorporated submitted a proposal to NASA under the NextSTEP-3 Lunar Enabling Infrastructure Accelerator program to advance the Astrotech Mobile Power System from TRL 4 to TRL 6.

The proposed lunar power system is designed to provide 6 kW of continuous power, with a 10 kW surge, in lunar polar environments. If selected, the project would include an integrated system test at Astrotech’s Austin facility.
Astrotech’s subsidiaries operate across trace detection, agricultural process analysis, industrial chemical process control, environmental testing and potential lunar infrastructure development.
